dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For x in Option (Option (Fin k)), this function equals c when x is none, computed when x is some none, and products(i) when x is some (some i).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its absolute values are summed over every nested-option value, giving exactly |c| + |computed| + sum_i |products(i)|.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the dependent three-way case eliminator for Option (Option (Fin k)): outer none uses h_1, outer some with inner none uses h_2, and outer some with inner some i uses h_3(i).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the three cases of LocalDef001 and ensures that its universal sum contains one c term, one computed term, and one term for each i in Fin k.

dependency_coverage.name: And

dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It requires the three families of perturbation bounds and the final perturbed equality to hold simultaneously.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin k is the finite type of natural-number indices i satisfying 0 <= i < k.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives products and theta_p exactly k indexed components; when k = 0, this index type is empty.

binders: For every natural number k, including k = 0.
For arbitrary real numbers u, computed, and c.
For an arbitrary family products : Fin k -> Real, equivalently k real numbers p_i indexed by i = 0, ..., k-1.
hypotheses: The residual satisfies |computed - (c - sum_i p_i)| <= ((k + 1)u)(|c| + |computed| + sum_i |p_i|), where every sum is over i in Fin k.
conclusions: There exist real numbers theta_0 and theta_c and a function theta_p : Fin k -> Real.
For every i in Fin k, |theta_p(i)| <= (k + 1)u.
They satisfy the exact identity computed(1 + theta_0) = c(1 + theta_c) - sum_i p_i(1 + theta_p(i)).
mathematical_definitions: Let S = sum_i p_i, with S = 0 when k = 0.
Let delta = ((k + 1) cast to a real number) times u.
The local nested-option function is g(none) = c, g(some none) = computed, and g(some (some i)) = p_i; hence sum_x |g(x)| = M.

The existential witnesses are syntactically introduced in the order theta_0, theta_c, theta_p. They may depend on all universally quantified inputs and both hypotheses; since no universal quantifier intervenes, this is equivalent to their joint existence.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural number k, all real numbers u, computed, and c, and every k-component real family p_i, if u is nonnegative and the absolute residual |computed - (c - sum_i p_i)| is at most (k + 1)u times |c| + |computed| + sum_i |p_i|, then one can assign separate relative perturbations to computed, c, and every p_i, each having absolute value at most (k + 1)u, so that the resulting multiplicatively perturbed equation computed(1 + theta_0) = c(1 + theta_c) - sum_i p_i(1 + theta_p(i)) holds exactly.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition is conditional. For inputs that do not satisfy the residual inequality, it makes no assertion and the implication is vacuously true.
Only nonnegative u is covered; negative u is excluded.
No smallness condition such as (k + 1)u < 1 is imposed, so the permitted relative perturbations need not be small.
When u = 0, the residual hypothesis forces computed = c - sum_i p_i, and all perturbations are forced to be zero by their bounds.
When k = 0, all sums over Fin k are empty, theta_p has an empty domain, its pointwise bound is vacuous, and the magnitude sum reduces to |c| + |computed|.
The residual scale contains k + 2 absolute-value terms, namely c, computed, and k product entries, while the perturbation bound is the distinct factor (k + 1)u.

The identifiers computed and products impose no computational semantics: the proposition does not state that computed arose from floating-point arithmetic or that products(i) are themselves products of other values.
There are no sign, positivity, nonzero, dimensional-vector, matrix, or probabilistic assumptions on c, computed, or the entries p_i.
At a zero-valued coefficient, its relative perturbation has no effect on the exact identity, although the perturbation variable is still required to satisfy its bound.
The perturbations need not be unique, equal to one another, independent of the data, or generated by any specified algorithm.
